title: The Dove and the Crow
summary: Inside the ornate courtyard of a wealthy merchant's villa, a pampered white dove lived inside an elaborate gilded wicker cage. Through unexpected trial and turning point, each character learns that multiplying children in captivity only multiplies the parent’s sorrow.
full_text: Inside the ornate courtyard of a wealthy merchant's villa, a pampered white dove lived inside an elaborate gilded wicker cage. Every morning, the master’s servants brought her fresh millet, clean spring water, and soft cotton for her nest, ensuring she was shielded from the cold winds and predators of the open world. Proud of her quiet shelter, the dove sat beside her nest and began boasting loudly to the wild birds gathered on the courtyard eaves: "Look upon my fruitful nest! I have hatched four fine broods of fledglings this season alone, more than any wild bird in the entire district! Is there any mother under heaven more blessed and productive than I?" A ragged wild crow, perched on the tiled roof of the stable, looked down through the wire bars with a gaze of sorrowful pity. "Why do you boast, foolish captive?" croaked the crow. "Every chick you bring forth into that cage will never know the freedom of soaring over mountain valleys or wheeling through the open sky. The more fledglings you hatch within your gilded bars, the more captives you provide to serve your master's amusement. To multiply children into servitude is no honor; true blessing lies in freedom, not in the abundance of one's chains."
moral: Multiplying children in captivity only multiplies the parent’s sorrow.
